svg.title: Normalization & Denormalization
svg.desc: Normalization & Denormalization. Store each fact once to keep data consistent, then copy some on purpose where reads must be fast, and keep the copies in step. Step 1, One wide table: Repeated facts: an email change rewrites 6,537 rows; inserts fail and deletes lose a customer. Step 2, Each fact stored once: Normal forms split it by what each column depends on: 4 tables, and the new email is UPDATE 1. Step 3, Copy on purpose: orders.total_thb is a deliberate copy kept by a trigger; the price paid is a fact, not a copy. Step 4, Joins vs copies: Joins cost reads, copies cost writes; document stores make the same choice as embed or reference.

g.text: Repeated facts: an email change rewrites 6,537 rows; inserts fail and deletes lose a customer.
Normal forms split it by what each column depends on: 4 tables, and the new email is UPDATE 1.
orders.total_thb is a deliberate copy kept by a trigger; the price paid is a fact, not a copy.
Joins cost reads, copies cost writes; document stores make the same choice as embed or reference.
UPDATE order_lines_wide SET email = 'customer1@example.org' WHERE customer_id = 1
CREATE TABLE orders (id bigint PRIMARY KEY, customer_id bigint REFERENCES customers, …)
UPDATE customers SET email = 'customer1@example.org' WHERE id = 1
SELECT id, created_at, status, total_thb FROM orders WHERE customer_id = 1
UPDATE products SET price_thb = 2799.00 WHERE id = 4077
SELECT … FROM orders o JOIN customers c JOIN order_items i JOIN products p … WHERE o.id = 41
INSERT INTO order_items SELECT id, 9, 4077, 1, 2646.15 FROM orders WHERE id > 490000
repeated: customer 1's email in 6,537 rows, Product 4077 in 111
one row per order line: 1,250,000 rows, 25,280 pages, 198 MB
one new email: UPDATE rewrote 6,537 rows
one value per cell: no list of products in one column
nothing depends on part of the key (order_id, line_no) → orders
nothing depends on a non-key column → customers, products
customer 1's new email has to be written into all 6,537 of their lines
miss some (WHERE order_id = 41 → UPDATE 2) and customer 1 has two emails
a new product, or a new price, has nowhere to go until someone orders it:
null value in column "order_id" … violates not-null constraint
and the 4,120 customers who never ordered can't be stored at all
DELETE order 124446 (3 lines), and customer 5797's email and country go too

g.text: Four ways to keep orders.total_thb right
AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE ON order_items
FOR EACH ROW: total_thb ± qty × price_thb
2 · application code, in the same transaction
each code path that writes order_items also updates orders
3 · materialized view instead of a column
REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW reruns the whole SUM
applies each committed item change to the copy
✓ check: 0 of 500,000 totals differ from the SUM of their lines
embed the lines: read with the order and owned by it
reference the customer: shared by 2,633 orders, changes alone
one Query on CUSTOMER#1 returns the customer and the orders
CQRS read models keep the copies in a separate store, fed by events
new email for customer 1, stored in
EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS, WAL), PostgreSQL 18.6, warm cache · wide table indexed on customer_id · WAL without full-page images
the same list, SUM over the lines
